oil.when: 2021, using the arrow and OK buttons on the steering wheel
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have been changed.
Turn the ignition on and bring up the main menu in the instrument cluster with the steering wheel display controls.
Scroll to Settings, press the right arrow, then scroll to Vehicle.
Press the right arrow again and scroll to Oil Life.
Press and hold OK while the cluster shows Hold OK to Reset.
Let go when it shows Reset Successful and the oil life reads 100%. If it says Not Reset or Reset Cancelled, go through the steps again.

oil.when: 2012, using the SETUP and RESET message center buttons
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have been changed.
Press and release SETUP until the message center shows OIL LIFE XXX% HOLD RESET = NEW.
Press and hold RESET for about two seconds, then let go. The oil life goes back to 100%.
oil.note: If you keep pressing RESET while OIL LIFE SET TO XXX% is showing, each press lowers the starting value by 10%. Stop at 100% unless you want shorter oil change intervals.

steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Drive for at least two minutes above 20 mph (32 km/h).
The light should go out by itself once the system reads the corrected pressures. There is no button to press.
If it stays on with the tires set correctly and the spare not in use, have the system checked.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about a minute at start-up and then stays on, the system has a fault that adding air will not fix. The manual also calls for a system reset after a tire rotation; ask the tire shop or dealer to do it if you are not sure how.

steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Drive for at least two minutes above 20 mph (32 km/h).
The light goes out by itself once the system reads the corrected pressures. There is no driver reset.
If the tires are set correctly, the spare is not in use and the light stays on, have a dealer check the system soon.
tpms.note: The light also stays on while the temporary spare is fitted, until the repaired tire goes back on. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.

notes: Navigator uses a calculated oil life reminder, so it does not clear itself after an oil change. The tire pressure light has no reset button on the years covered here; it clears after a short drive once the tires are set right.
